rules.name: Upgrade Ant javac source/target from 1.5 to 1.6
rules.description: Ant build.xml specifies javac source=1.5 and target=1.5. These must be updated to 1.6.

patterns.reason: Update Java source and target compatibility from 1.5 to 1.6

rules.verification_hint: Check that build.xml javac tasks use source=1.6 and target=1.6 and compilation succeeds on Java 6.

blast_class_evidence.reasoning: All real sites are Ant <javac> source/target and <javacc> jdkversion/target attribute values in build.xml -- a build-tool file no .java source ever reads -- so the change can never alter a field type, a return type, a parameter type, or an implements/extends list, and the site list is cross-checked exactly against 03-build-fixes-plan.json, so the rule is classified body-local with high confidence.

sites.what_changes: The javac task attribute source="1.5" becomes source="1.6" (already applied in this workspace, the line now reads source="1.6"); it is an Ant compiler flag inside a single <javac> element, it declares no Java type and no .java file references it.

The javac task attribute target="1.5" becomes target="1.6" on the same <javac> element that compiles ${src} into ${build}; it only changes the emitted class-file version, not any signature in the sources.

The <javacc> attribute pair jdkversion/target in target MakeACLParser is rewritten to 1.6; it changes only the generated-parser toolchain level for src/jade/lang/acl, and the generated classes keep their existing public API.
The <javacc> attribute target in target StandAloneMakeExtendedSLParser is rewritten to 1.6; same scope as line 129, a build-tool attribute with no Java-level consumer.

rules.name: Java 6 enforces stricter cast checking per JLS
rules.description: Java SE 6 casts adhere more closely to JLS. Previously accepted incorrect programs may be rejected by Java 6 javac.

patterns.reason: Java 6 enforces stricter cast rules. Complex casts should be reviewed.

rules.verification_hint: Compile with Java 6 javac and ensure no new type incompatibility errors appear.

blast_class_evidence.reasoning: Although most of the 2548 flagged sites are local-variable assignments or scanner false positives, three genuine casts sit in method return position -- one of them, PlatformManagerStub.findSlice, implementing the PlatformManager interface contract -- so per the mixed-rule tie-break the rule is classified signature, with confidence kept at medium because its recipe is unregistered in recipe-registry.json and today falls back to a no-op.

sites.what_changes: The cast in 'return (Service.Slice)localSlices.get(serviceName);' is the whole body of 'protected Service.Slice getSlice(String serviceName)', so the cast type is identical to the declared return type; retyping the cast forces the method return type to change, which propagates to the 15 files calling getSlice( and to the 2 subclasses NodeLEAP and NodeAdapter that extend BaseNode.

'return (Service.Slice) res.getParamAt(0);' is the return of 'public Service.Slice findSlice(String serviceKey, String sliceKey)', a method implementing the PlatformManager contract; changing the cast type changes the return type of an interface-implementing method, so the interface declaration and the 11 files referencing findSlice( must change too.

'return (FIPA.MTS) that;' sits inside the public static CORBA helper 'public static FIPA.MTS narrow(org.omg.CORBA.Object that)'; the cast type equals the declared return type of a public API entry point, so any retype is a public signature change visible to every caller of MTSHelper.narrow.

'previous = (BackEndContainer.AgentImage) myContainer.addAgentImage(agentID, image);' assigns into the local variable declared as 'Agent previous = null;' at line 169; a retype here stays inside the method body, so this site alone would be body-local.

'current = (AgentTree.Node) selPath.getLastPathComponent();' assigns into the local 'AgentTree.Node current;' declared at line 65 inside 'private JPopupMenu getPopup(MouseEvent e)'; the change cannot leave the method body.
Nothing changes: the flagged line is 'if(logger.isLoggable(Logger.CONFIG))' and the manifest regex matched the argument list '(Logger.CONFIG)', not a cast; this is a scanner false positive.
Nothing changes: the flagged line is 'out.write_string(that.name);' and the regex matched the qualified field read '(that.name)' used as a call argument, not a cast expression.
